evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 字形; 形義源流通解; 《說文》; 《詩》; 《公羊傳》
evidence.text: The entry displays one bronze form, one seal form, and four manuscript examples, with no oracle-bone example shown. It analyzes the bronze form as 水 plus phonetic 曷 and says the graph was later written 竭 for ‘water drying up’; it cites the Zhongshan King Fanghu and a Mawangdui Laozi manuscript for the exhausted/dried-up usage. It separately cites 詩·王風·君子于役 for ‘thirsty’, Tang Bai Juyi for ‘dry/parched’, and 公羊傳·隱公三年 for ‘urgent’. The page does not establish the exact date of the earliest physical witness of the Shijing line or dated intermediate stages linking ‘exhausted’ to ‘thirsty’. These are the database’s readings of the forms and texts; I did not visually inspect the glyph images.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 渴

evidence.source: 小學堂字形演變資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.text: The official user guide describes the database as a search tool that gathers representative forms from oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, seal-script, and other collections, with source and form-analysis information. Its guide cautions that the ordering of forms is not always chronological. I did not obtain a character-specific 渴 record from the database in this search.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK’s 渴 page and Academia Sinica’s Xiaoxuetang database page. Search surfaced a Wiktionary file lead for a Warring States bronze-style rendering of 渴, but Commons and the direct asset could not be opened.

search_audit.query: "渴-bronze-warring.svg" license; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 渴 bronze warring svg; 小學堂字形演變 CC0 1.0 rights notice
search_audit.outcome: Commons page for the exact 渴 file and Xiaoxuetang terms URL were inaccessible. The guide was opened and verified database scope; it did not establish a character-specific form or image URL. Other Commons results concerned different characters and were not used.

gaps: No usable direct image URL with verified identity and reuse provenance was established. The candidate渴-bronze-warring.svg file page and asset could not be opened; no Xiaoxuetang record for 渴 or its specific glyph image was retrieved. Therefore no glyph image is proposed.
The CUHK page reports no oracle-bone example in its displayed entry; this does not establish absence from all oracle-bone corpora.

The cited Shijing thirsty use, exhaustion/drying use, parching use, and urgency use are separately recorded by CUHK, but exact earliest surviving witness dates and the semantic transition stages are not established here.

Fresh browsing in this invocation verified graphic and semantic evidence but did not independently verify readings or inspect the local Baxter–Sagart and Unihan rows. The packet’s reported unavailable official Unihan character lookups remain a limitation.

limitations.text: No image is selected because the candidate file page and image URL could not be accessed to establish direct asset URL, glyph identity, source attribution, and reuse rights. Xiaoxuetang is a relevant database lead, but no character-specific image record was obtained. Commons and Xiaoxuetang attempts and outcomes are recorded in search_audit.
